outline.chapter_title: Foundations: From Classical LSTMs to Modern Challenges
outline.description: This chapter establishes the historical context of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), focusing on the original Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture. It details the core mechanisms of the constant error carousel and gating, then critically analyzes the three fundamental limitations that prevented LSTMs from scaling to the level of modern Transformers: inability to revise storage decisions, limited scalar memory capacity, and lack of parallelizability.
subtopics: The Vanishing Gradient Problem and the Birth of LSTM
Anatomy of the Original LSTM Cell: Input, Forget, and Output Gates
The Constant Error Carousel Mechanism
Limitation I: The Inability to Revise Storage Decisions
Limitation II: Scalar Memory Bottlenecks and Information Compression
Limitation III: Sequential Dependencies and Lack of Parallelization
The Rise of Transformers and State Space Models as Alternatives

outline.chapter_title: Core Innovation I: Exponential Gating and Stabilization
outline.description: This chapter dives into the first major modification introduced by xLSTM: replacing standard sigmoid gating with exponential gating. It explains how this change empowers the network to dynamically revise past storage decisions, effectively solving the 'nearest neighbor' revision problem. The chapter also covers the mathematical necessity of normalization and stabilization techniques to prevent numerical overflow inherent in exponential functions.
subtopics: Motivation for Exponential Activation Functions in Gates
Mathematical Formulation of Exponential Input and Forget Gates
The Normalizer State: Tracking Cumulative Gate Strengths
Stabilization Techniques: Log-Sum-Exp Tricks and Max-State Tracking
Proof of Equivalence: Stability Without Altering Gradients
Impact on Revising Stored Information in Synthetic Tasks

outline.chapter_title: Core Innovation II: The sLSTM Architecture
outline.description: Focusing on the scalar variant of xLSTM, this chapter details the design of the sLSTM. It explores how sLSTM retains the traditional scalar memory cell but enhances it with exponential gating and a novel memory mixing strategy involving multiple heads. The chapter clarifies how sLSTM addresses state-tracking problems that pure attention or diagonal state-space models cannot solve.
subtopics: sLSTM Forward Pass Derivation
Scalar Memory Updates with Exponential Forgetting
Novel Memory Mixing: Hidden-to-Hidden Connections in sLSTM
Multi-Head Configurations within sLSTM Blocks
State Tracking Capabilities: Solving Formal Language Tasks
Trade-offs: Expressivity vs. Sequential Computation

outline.chapter_title: Core Innovation III: The mLSTM Architecture
outline.description: This chapter introduces the matrix variant, mLSTM, designed to maximize storage capacity and enable parallelization. It explains the transition from scalar states to matrix memories using a covariance update rule (Key-Value outer products). Students will learn how mLSTM mimics associative memory mechanisms, removes hidden-hidden recurrence to allow parallel training, and integrates query-key-value projections similar to attention mechanisms.
subtopics: From Scalar to Matrix Memory: Increasing Storage Capacity
The Covariance Update Rule: Storing Key-Value Pairs
Connection to Bidirectional Associative Memories (BAMs)
